s0.p2: Go to the **Sources** tab of the developer panel:
s0.p3: On the left we see the navigation panel:
s0.p4:
To view the code of the loaded page, use the button **⟦f1⟧** and open **_Pages_**.
Now you can see the project structure in the navigation panel and you can select a file to view.
Select the project file, the contents of which will be displayed in the center (**index02.js**).
s0.p5: On the right side you see the panel of the debugger itself:
s0.p6: You can work not only with the code of an open page in the debugger.
s0.p7: You can create your own piece of code that you want to debug.
s0.p8: Using the same **⟦f1⟧** button in the navigation panel, select **_Snippets_**.
s0.p9: **Snippet** - is a piece of code that is stored in the browser for quite a long time under the name you give it.
s0.p10: To add a new code fragment, click on the button •• + New Snippet •• in the left navigation bar and give your snippet a title.
s0.p11:
Next, you can paste the snippet code in the center, save the changes (Ctrl+S) and run the snippet code for execution ► **Ctrl + Enter**.

^^If the changes have not been saved, then the modified snippet will be displayed in the navigation panel (on the left) marked with ⟦f2⟧.^^
s0.p12: The most important sections of the debugger that you will need to master first are:
s0.p13: To track the values ​​of variables, we use the section **Watch**.
s0.p14: In this section you can add the names of the variables whose values ​​you want to track.
s0.p15: But in order to see how these values ​​change during code execution, you need to set **⟦f6⟧**.
s0.p16:
This is quite easy to do directly in the snippet code.
All lines of code are numbered, and just click on the line number to set a breakpoint.
s0.p17: After running the snippet (► **Ctrl + Enter**) , the engine will execute line by line until it reaches the next **⟦f9⟧**.
s0.p18: Here the engine will pause executing the code, and you will be able to see the current values ​​of the variables you are watching, and then resume executing the code from where you left off.
s0.p19: You can also make changes to the code, save your changes (**⟦f5⟧**) and resume code execution.
s0.p20: After resuming, the new version of the code will work.
s0.p21: To resume the execution of the code, use the button ![ico-40 debug-button].
s0.p22: ![ico-25 warn] After setting the ⟦f6⟧, you need to reload the page ![reload].
s0.p23: ![ico20] You can also track changes in variable values in the **⟦f7⟧** section of the debugger:
s0.p24: • Local - local variables of the function being executed.
s0.p25: • Block - variables of the call context of the executable function.
s1.p1: In **Chrome DevTools**, you can also suspend code execution when DOM events occur.
